verdict.rationale: Unreal documents its own APIs: a generated per-class Python API reference, Python stub generation for autocomplete, C++ programming guides and Remote Control HTTP/WebSocket references, much of it fetchable by non-browser clients. That is partial support for the 'well-documented APIs' part of the story. Nothing in the pack shows LLM-generated Unreal code working on the first try or a large body of public examples. The Python API is marked Experimental, and probes report source access is EULA-gated, docs are not served as markdown, and the CDN intermittently blocks agents. missing for 10: evidence that LLM-generated code works first-try, evidence of abundant public code examples, evidence of API stability across versions, reliable machine-readable docs and source access.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen
